content: The nasal bones are two small, elongated bones that vary in size and shape among individuals. They are positioned side by side at the midline and upper part of the face, forming the bridge of the nose where they meet. Each nasal bone has two distinct surfaces and four borders. The outer surface of the nasal bone is concavoconvex when viewed from top to bottom and convex from side to side. This surface is covered by the Procerus and Compressor naris muscles. Near the center of the outer surface, there is a foramen that allows the passage of a small vein. The inner surface of the nasal bone is concave from side to side. It features a groove that runs vertically from top to bottom, which accommodates a branch of the nasociliary nerve. The nasal bones articulate with four other bones. Two of these are cranial bones: the frontal bone and the ethmoid bone. The other two are facial bones: the opposite nasal bone and the maxilla.
